caption: The drawing depicts an organized garden or park layout from an aerial perspective, featuring multiple rectangular and square sections bordered by green lines. Each section contains intricate patterns and geometric designs rendered in varying shades of green, blue, and yellow, with some areas marked by dot-like shapes suggesting plants or flowers. Several sections display symmetrical, ornamental motifs while others contain rows or circular arrangements. Along the right edge, a row of evenly spaced green trees is shown. On the lower right, there are a few pinkish rectangular structures, likely representing buildings, situated adjacent to a pale tan area that forms a pathway or open space connecting the sections. The entire garden is bordered by different green shaded regions, with the left side appearing more densely filled and the right side containing open, grassy land interspersed with brown earth and additional green foliage. The colors primarily include various greens, blues, yellows, and pinks, and the composition is arranged with a clear grid-like structure.
title: Ranelagh Gardens
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
